title: Hovering a name in a report chart legend shows latest month and average
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. At least two technicians appear in this location's Technician Efficiency and Technician Utilization charts (they have clocked time in the period you look at). At least two service advisors appear in this location's Billing Efficiency / Advisor Analysis chart (they have invoiced work with clocked time in the period you look at).
  3. You use a desktop browser at 100% zoom on a screen at least 1024 pixels wide (any ordinary laptop or desktop monitor).
  4. On each report below, the chart is shown (click Show chart if it is hidden).
custom_steps:
1. Click Reports in the top bar and click Advisor Analysis in the left menu.
  2. Hover one advisor's name in the legend above the chart (any advisor in the list) and read the box that appears.
  3. Hover that advisor's last point on the chart and read its value and month.
  4. Click Technician Efficiency and hover a technician's name in the legend (any technician in the legend).
  5. Click Technician Utilization and hover a technician's name in the legend (any technician in the list).
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The box shows the person's name, a large percent, and below it a month and an average (e.g. the advisor's name, 120%, Aug 2026 · avg 107%).
  • The large percent and the month match the person's latest point with a value on the chart.
  • The same box appears on the Technician Efficiency and Technician Utilization report charts (e.g. the technician's name, 70%, Aug 2026 · avg 95%).
  • Write the average and the person's figure from the report table in the result comment. Do not pass or fail on the average: whether it must equal the table's figure is an open question for the product owner.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9583 (Story 11, Chart on the Report Page); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 11. This readout is shown in the design only; the PRD does not describe it.
